editorial.headline: Animal Cosmetics Manufacturing, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20233 covers the making of animal cosmetics, a nationally open activity that the Bali record blocks for PMA registration under its risk-class moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20233 is a manufacturing activity for cosmetics made for animals. The record describes its scope as the production of animal-use cosmetic goods, including perfume, shampoo, soap, powder, cream, lotion, and similar products. In plain English, this is not retailing, grooming, veterinary treatment, or pet-care services; it is the factory-side activity of making cosmetic products intended for animals. The emphasis is on production: turning formulas, ingredients, packaging, and manufacturing process into finished animal cosmetic goods.

The scale profile is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, which means the classification is not confined to one size of enterprise. A small producer and a larger industrial manufacturer can both sit inside the same activity description, provided what they do is the making of animal cosmetics. That matters because the KBLI question is not whether the business feels boutique or industrial in branding terms, but whether the registered activity matches the manufacturing scope in the record.

Nationally, the investment position is straightforward: the record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national reading, therefore, this is a foreign-open activity, not a closed one, and the maximum foreign stake shown in the record is the full percentage. Nothing in the slim record adds a licence condition, tax threshold, capital threshold, operational deadline, or special permit narrative beyond that national status, so the clean national conclusion is simply that KBLI 20233 is open to foreign ownership up to 100%.

Bali is the decisive exception. The record marks Bali as Blocked (risk class) and says l4_bali_blocked is true. Its reason is explicit: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026". The moratorium rule is also explicit: "Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)". The honest reading is therefore not that Bali has a different foreign-ownership percentage, but that PMA registration for this activity is blocked in Bali under the recorded moratorium. A foreign-owned company may see a nationally open 100% figure, but for Bali today the practical answer in this record is no registration.
